cards.note: Ships as an npm package with dsh.bundle.patch + a cordis.patch.yml insert row (cordis.patch.yml); it never used the removed repository-plugin mechanism, so there is nothing to convert and the official profile path is already the only one.
No legacy dshClient field or dsh.plugin.json exists in the source or in the baseline commit; the client half is declared under dsh.client.

dsh.client declares platform 'web' and the package exports the ./client bundle, which is exactly the alpha.2 scan precondition (client-modules parseDshClient + clientExportOf); without both the browser half stays out of the boot graph.

Every property-accessed service is declared: client inject ['slots','locale','sessions'], host inject ['webServer','connection'] (index.js). The only undeclared services are optional and read through ctx.get, which on cordis 4.0.2 returns undefined instead of tripping the proxy.

ctx.get('documentTitle') and ctx.get('betterLocale') are weak probes with graceful degradation; hard inject entries are reserved for services guaranteed by the web profile (index.js adds 'connection' for the gate).
The plugin never subscribes to session/event and never reads event.kind/type; its only session read is the sessions.list metadata snapshot.

The rc.1-era absence of ctx.sessions is gone on alpha.2: @deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller/client provides the sessions service (SessionListState with current/byId) and the web bundle mounts its row, so the documented title writer keeps its client-side read instead of moving aggregation into the Node half.
No tasks/jobs output is tailed; the host half serves only its own HTTP route and settings namespace.
The HTTP service was already the renamed webServer and still is on alpha.2 (webServer.register({kind:'prefix'}) keeps its shape); no tasks/onTaskDone usage exists.
No ImageAttachmentRef/read_image metadata is produced or persisted by this plugin.
The plugin neither registers nor parses read_image; nothing matches on its content string.
No custom DeepSeek adapter, image interceptor, or attachment cache exists in this plugin.
No APIProxy call site: the host half uses its own gated HTTP route and the settings service; there is no ctx.remote consumer to migrate.
The plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents, and the target is alpha.2 (A2-01 restores ignorable), so the alpha.1-only condition is not met.
No host source patch imports internal session-view paths; the single shipped patch touches packages/client/ui-layout's title projection only.
No launcher/SDK wrapper and no hardcoded user directory: the plugin's own cordis.patch.yml is a bundle patch layer resolved by the official launcher/profile.
Not a headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser; no dsh: reasoning: segment handling applies.
No tool presentation mode, PTC preset, or dispatch waterfall usage.
Not a permission/approval/WebFetch policy or audit plugin; it uses neither the shipped presets nor web_fetch.

The custom route /bench-brand-text/api is now gate-first: the handler calls ctx.connection.requestRejection(req) before dispatch (401 no browser session, 403 Host/Origin fence) and the plugin hard-injects 'connection' beside 'webServer', because webServer routes inherit no authentication.
Not a model provider plugin; it registers no provider login configuration.

The plugin registers its own zh/en dictionaries through the official ctx.locale.register and ships no custom language or i18n patch; the optional betterLocale probe integrates a third-party override service, which alpha.2's addLanguage (language registration) does not replace.
No subagent orchestration or selector surface.
Informational deployment/privacy surface: the plugin is not an LLM adapter, and its code needs no change for the adapter's package-name/version reporting.
No persistent PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker workarounds exist to retire.
The plugin does not use the official DeepSeek LLM API and enables no session-log-deepseek egress.

The browser acceptance lane opens the token launch URL (DSH_MIGRATE_WEB_URL, letting the redirect issue the cookie), reads window.__DSH_BOOT__.entries from the real page, finds the entry by package.json#name, requests the advertised client artifact, and asserts the __ModuleLoader__.load registration; helpers.ts carries the manifest/registration readers.
No structured-question answerer is registered; userQuestions/registerProvider is unused.
No agent-preset inference or preset roots are used.
isTokenDelta / first-token TPS computation is not used anywhere in the plugin.
The bundle layer only inserts its own row; it does not reuse or restate the dsh-base composition's telemetry rows, so the changed defaults and the package-inventory row are not its surface.
The plugin does not import @earendil-works/pi-ai or any provider/auth adapter package.

The rc.8 cohort's @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime is gone from the peer list, dsh.client.inject, and the store engine: createSnapshotStore now comes from the client baseline @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store, and the context type from @deepseek-ai/cordis plus type-only /client augmentations.

The served client artifact is now a self-registering closure-factory bundle: window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: '@bench/dsh-bench-brand-text', factory }), the id equal to package.json#name (the boot-graph/module-table key). The assembly row in cordis.patch.yml already uses the bare package name, so all three ids agree.
The plugin reads only the sessions.list metadata snapshot (session title), never per-session conversation nodes, timelines, or user message content, so the SessionBinding event window is not needed.
No composer DOM manipulation (draft injection, history recall, selection) exists in the plugin.
The settings card uses plain form fields and renders no MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock from ui-primitives.

No ctx.connection.api consumer on the client plane: the browser half reads ctx.sessions.list for the title and talks to the plugin's own route; the new host-plane ctx.connection use is the A1-08 gate, a different face.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptors or subagent/descriptor consumers.
Workspace navigation/list is not used; no connectWorkspace/startSession/pickDirectory calls or baselinesReady reads.
The plugin writes no third-party persisted SessionEvents, so the restored ignorable retention semantics have no producer here.
No ctx.remote or Remote unary call sites; the card's RemoteResult/RemoteError handling has nothing to apply to.

Peer cohort re-pinned to ^0.1.2-alpha.2 (cordis ^4.0.2, schemastery ^3.18.1, react ^18.2.0), every dsh peer verified present at the alpha.2 tag, dsh-client-runtime removed, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection added for the host-half gate, and peerDependenciesMeta mirrors the list; dsh.client.external stays empty because only baseline modules are value-imported.
No startup wrapper or CI matrix workaround (no forced Node 22, no skipped dsh web, no loader-major probe) exists in the plugin.

The plugin never consumes pluginInventory/list or validates PluginInventorySnapshot; the acceptance lane reads the host's rendered Plugins page, so optional agentPresets grouping is the host UI's concern.
The client half does not call host.describe and has no $host.home/isLoopback read or reconnect polling.
The plugin composes no tool packages individually; it is one bundle row on the shipped profile, so the sessionProjections inject/peer requirement does not reach it.

The namespace is a bare literal constant (SETTINGS_NAMESPACE = 'bench-brand-text') passed to the settings register/installSection seam; no runtime settingsNamespace() import or helper survives, matching the compile-time SettingsNamespaceInput validation.
